observations.B01: Authorial page number reads 31, with two lobes in 3 and a separate upright 1.
observations.B02: The first word has d, apostrophe, and a very compressed final low sequence; d’ici and d’où remain alternatives. The middle word after en has a tall d and several low s/u-like strokes, but dessus versus dehors is not settled by them. The final ring has a double-stroked Z, square brackets, and literal 1/2. A tiny top-edge ink tip is excluded as neighboring material.
observations.B03: Equation number 79 and the two-row brace are clear. The unstruck fractions are 1/2, minus 1/12 in the upper row, and plus 5/12 in the lower row. The capital in both parenthetical terms has a horizontal top and hooked lower stem, so T/J remains explicitly uncertain. Crosshatching obscures both abandoned expressions; the listed readings are tentative stroke readings, especially the final alpha-like mark above and the denominator 3-like remnant below. The added bracketed M has an angular hat and a separate infinity superscript. Two short vertical equality strokes and 1/2 appear directly under that term and are retained as a downward annotation.
observations.B04: The phrase reads Voici un autre calcul de, followed by bracketed M with two subscript ones. The lower line begins considère le morphisme modulaire; the p descender and h ascender in morphisme are visible.
observations.B05: The target has plain M with subscript 1,1, a rightward arrow, and double-stemmed E. Its raised stroke reads numeral 1, consistent with the explicitly shaped numeral over E elsewhere on this same page, rather than a prime.
observations.B06: The opening et is crossed through; on follows separately. The verb has a tall initial d, a compressed middle, and a p-like descender, leaving décompose/découpe uncertain. Double-stemmed E has superscript 1. S-zero is thickly retraced. The lower line ends with elliptique at the crop boundary.
observations.B07: The opening h and terminal descending q support harmonique. The abbreviation after groupe begins d’auto and ends with a low hook, read d’autos. The quotient has numeral 4 between the slash and the final double-stroked Z.
observations.B08: S-one is visible at the left. A small a-like shape and a heavily hatched cluster follow; a Z/slash/3-like fragment is tentative and kept within the deletion. The parenthetical wording after courbe is compressed and remains uncertain: the pair of tall loops supports ell., while the following word has a tall initial and low final humps. Avec un gr. is more secure. The top-edge descender from harmonique is excluded.
observations.B09: The quotient denominator is 6. The following words have the descenders of qui and coupent. The lower line reads qu’en les pts 2 et 3, qui correspondent; the last word meets the right boundary but its terminal t is present. Pts is left abbreviated.
observations.B10: The parenthesis has the long f descender of sauf, then erreur. The following phrase is à des groupes d’autos. The isolated top-left descender belongs to the line above and is excluded.
observations.B11: The two numbers read 24 and 12. The sentence continues On a donc une partition. In the formula a crossed double-stemmed E-like glyph precedes U. The first two union-like signs have horizontal bases and are recorded as amalgamation; the last two are plain cups. S-zero and S-one carry primes, with no separate exclamation dot. A small top-edge fragment from the preceding line is excluded.
observations.B12: The lead où is followed by a short cancellation, tentatively on a. The mark between E-superscript-one and the parenthesis is crossed or diagonal and can be read as set-minus or plus; it has not been corrected from the intended set relation. The brace groups the point-intersection equation and the two primed-S definitions. Short vertical guides attach a2 and a3 to car 2 and car 3 below. In the S-zero-prime definition the first subscript is shaped more like 3 than the earlier 2, so both are retained rather than normalizing the set. The later S-one-prime definition reads a2,a3. All prime marks are separate short strokes.
observations.B13: Separate pencil foliation reads 63. The second digit has two open lobes, and the first has an enclosed lower loop. The dark page-border strip is excluded.
